For a stored complex column $x\in\mathbb C^m$, $m\ge1$, and block $B\in\mathbb C^{m\times q}$, $q\ge0$, call the Householder branch of [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] on $[x\;B]$. This is the canonical scaled real-component norm and separately scaled phase-modulus realization, with fixed sequential dots, real-coefficient multiplication, complex product and subtraction order. It includes the exact target-column overwrite. Return its $(v,\widehat\tau,\widehat\alpha,\widehat x,\widehat B)$ on success; a zero column returns identity, zero column and copied $B$. Report an invalid/nonpositive stored-vector norm as `breakdown`; every other invalid/out-of-range operation returns `range-failure` with its operation index and partial values.

The exact representative is $P(v)=I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$ for nonzero stored $v$. Store this product representation rather than identifying the rounded rank-one action with an exactly unitary dense matrix. For polynomial-vector initialization, form the reflector from that external vector and use its separate-block application on the entire active row panel; do not overwrite an unrelated matrix column. The proof-backed target and separate-block coefficients are supplied by [[lem-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-local-backward-error]].

The verification/controller model is an exact real-RAM: its scalar field operations $+,-,\times,/$, zero/order comparisons, finite indices and copies act on the exact input/stored real values. Complex controller operations mean their real-component field formulas. The final audit uses the fixed row-major loops for $M\widehat X-C$, with inner products summed in increasing index order, and tests all real/imaginary components for zero. These are prescribed finite expression trees/loops, not an unprovided certification oracle. No implementation or bit-cost claim for arbitrary real encodings is made. In a rational adapter, exact rational inputs and a supplied finite format codebook give every stored real code its exact rational value; decoding is finite table lookup. When all required codes/values are supplied, the same audit is finite exact rational arithmetic (binary formats give dyadic values). Missing/invalid adapter data return `representation-inconclusive`; they are not silently assumed. The default exact real-RAM route requires no rational/dyadic decoder.

Candidate operations use
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Charge one budget unit BEFORE each rounded real primitive, including each component conversion and every primitive inside a called norm, reflector, complex product, subtraction or division. On exhaustion return `budget-exhausted` with any available partial candidate. Successful exact controller operations, index loops, comparisons, conjugations and copies are separate from this rounded-operation budget; their loops are finite and no total cubic or bit-cost assertion is made here. Each excluded rounded intermediate returns `range-failure` with its index and partial values. Required stored scalar constants must be admissible, or the candidate route returns `candidate-failure`.

Replace each requested rounded real primitive or component conversion by the following dispatcher. With counter $b$ initially zero, first test $b=K$; if equal, return `budget-exhausted` immediately without evaluating that primitive. Otherwise increase $b$ by one and execute exactly that one primitive in the source arithmetic model; propagate its first failure. **Scalar execution order.** These conventions expand every arithmetic
expression below into a fixed finite scalar schedule; they do not execute the
exact theoretical representatives. Visit vector indices increasingly and matrix
columns increasingly, with row indices increasing within each column. Visit the
real component before the imaginary component. For a complex vector $z$, its
real-component list is $(\Re z_1,\Im z_1,\ldots,\Re z_r,\Im z_r)$.
Evaluate displayed assignments in their written order and nested operations
from the inside out, left operand before right operand. For inputs $a+ib$ and
$c+id$ with real components $a,b,c,d$, a complex product uses
rounded real products $ac,bd,ad,bc$, in that order, followed by the rounded real
subtraction $ac-bd$ and rounded imaginary addition $ad+bc$. Do not fuse
operations. Return immediately at the first failing primitive; indices refer
to this expanded order. Copies, sign changes and conjugations are exact.

For a scaled norm, first form every rounded component divided by the common
scale in list order. Then, in that same order, round each component square and
accumulate it: copy the first square to the accumulator, and round each
subsequent accumulator-plus-square addition. Use this same square-and-sum
schedule for the stored-vector squared norm $w$, without scaling. An empty
sum is exact zero and requests no primitive. Apply square root and rescaling
only at their prescribed subsequent stages. The two-component and
four-component norm calls use their displayed component lists in this order.

For the Householder dot row $d$, visit columns $j$ increasingly. For each
column visit $i=1,\ldots,r$, form the declared complex product
$\overline v_iB_{ij}$, copy the first product as the partial dot, then add each
later product by rounded real-component addition followed by rounded
imaginary-component addition. Finish all of $d$ before forming $p$ in
increasing row order, then all of $Z$ in the matrix order above, then all
entries of $B-Z$ in that order. Evaluate both components of the formation of
$v$ and every scalar scaling or division in real-then-imaginary order. A
separate block call uses already stored $v,\widehat\tau$ and the same
$d,p,Z,B-Z$ stages, omitting formation and target overwrite.

For a Givens application, visit columns increasingly and copy the two old
entries before changing either. Compute the upper output first, then the
lower output, each by its two products in written order followed by its
componentwise addition. Each of the prescribed two complex products uses
the six-operation schedule above, including a real coefficient viewed as a
complex number with zero imaginary component. Both outputs use the copied
old entries.
Perform an instructed target zero write only after these outputs. Right
applications execute the stated conjugate-transpose reduction with these
same conventions. No intermediate is reused across different expressions
unless explicitly stored by the procedure.

Use the operationwise real/complex arithmetic model, with six-real-operation complex products and componentwise division by positive real scalars. A scaled norm of a nonzero complex vector first chooses the largest absolute real or imaginary component $s>0$, rounds every real component divided by $s$, sums their rounded squares sequentially, rounds the positive square root, and rounds multiplication by $s$. A norm of already scaled components omits the last multiplication. Zero input has exact norm zero. Reject every nonzero exact intermediate outside the normal range, nonfinite/invalid operation, and nonpositive required norm; return the first range-failure. All sign changes and conjugations are exact.

For a Householder active block $C=[x\;B]$, $x\in\mathbb C^r$, a zero $x$ copies the block with identity action. Otherwise compute $\widehat N$ by the scaled norm. If $x_1=0$ put $\widehat\phi=1$; otherwise compute its modulus $\widehat a$ by its own two-component scaled norm and divide its real and imaginary parts by $\widehat a$. Set $\widehat\alpha=-\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\phi\widehat N)$ using real-scalar component multiplication, and $v=\operatorname{fl}(x-\widehat\alpha e_1)$. Compute $w$ by sequential summation of all $2r$ rounded real component squares of $v$, and $\widehat\tau=\operatorname{fl}(2/w)$. Compute $d=\operatorname{fl}(v^*B)$, $p=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\tau v)$, $Z=\operatorname{fl}(pd)$, and $\widehat B=\operatorname{fl}(B-Z)$. Return $C_+=[\widehat\alpha e_1\;\widehat B]$, writing exact zeros below the target diagonal, and store $v,\widehat\tau$. Its theoretical representative is $H(v)=I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$. For a separate block application omit the column overwrite. For a right step apply these instructions to the conjugate-transposed block and transpose back.

For a Givens target pair $(a,b)$, use the identity when $b=0$, including $(0,0)$. Otherwise choose $\lambda$ as the largest absolute real/imaginary component of $(a,b)$, round $z=a/\lambda$ and $w=b/\lambda$ componentwise, and compute $h$ as the norm of their four already scaled components. If $z\ne0$, compute $n_z$ as the norm of its two components, $\widehat\phi=\operatorname{fl}(z/n_z)$, $c=\operatorname{fl}(n_z/h)$ and $s=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\phi\overline w)/h)$. If $z=0$, set $c=0$ and $s=\operatorname{fl}(\overline w/h)$. Store $T=\begin{pmatrix}c&s\\-\overline s&c\end{pmatrix}$ and apply it to the chosen two rows using two complex products and one rounded componentwise addition for each output entry. For an actual target column, set its intended annihilated entry to exact zero after the update. The initial shift-vector rotation is formed from the shift vector but applied to the matrix without zeroing an unrelated matrix entry. Right applications use the conjugate-transposed form. Its exact unitary representative is $Q=T/\sqrt{c^2+|s|^2}$; this normalization defines a mathematical representative and is not an additional rounded operation.

These are arithmetic realizations of the canonical Householder and Givens methods. Returned dense transformation accumulators may be rounded; the exact unitary products used in backward-error statements are represented by the stored local data. Additional discarded matrix entries must be recorded separately, including their magnitudes. Their omission is never implicit in a sparsity convention.

Every scalar operation is evaluated in the operationwise model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. 2. At each sweep, test every active first-subdiagonal entry by
   $$|h_{i,i-1}|\le\tau\bigl(|h_{i-1,i-1}|+|h_{i,i}|\bigr).$$
   For a complex entry $z=a+ib$, evaluate $|z|$ by $s=\max(|a|,|b|)$ and $s\sqrt{(a/s)^2+(b/s)^2}$ when $z\ne0$, with divisions, squares, sum, square root and final scaling rounded in the stated order; use $|0|=0$. Every scalar operation is evaluated in the operationwise model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Any invalid, overflow, or underflow operation returns range-failure with the operation index and partial factors.

For each stored reflector with active indices $S=(s_1,\ldots,s_m)$, vector $v\in\mathbb F^m$, and real computed coefficient $\widehat\tau$, the real or complex formation routine first performs the stated finite left application. Each complex product uses the six real operations of the arithmetic model. The exact factor appended to $Q$ is $P(v)=I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$; the computed right update uses $\widehat\tau$ as displayed and is not asserted equal to multiplication by $P(v)$. For a matrix-target column, the formation routine's explicit zero writes are retained. In the initial polynomial-vector step there is no matrix-target column: use the entire active row panel for the left update and then apply the right update to the active columns. Record deflation writes separately, including a pure deflation with no following reflector as an identity-transform stage; a local error certificate must account for all other rounding and target-column writes.

For $k=1,\ldots,\max(n-2,0)$ in increasing order, use active indices $S=\{k+1,\ldots,n\}$, target $x=H_{S,k}$, and trailing left panel $B=H_{S,\{k+1,\ldots,n\}}$ with columns in increasing order. In the real branch use [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] for the finite left application and overwrite; in the complex branch use [[alg-complex-scaled-householder-reflector-step]]. Complete each similarity by the right application above on columns $S$. If the resulting matrix fails the exact upper-Hessenberg zero-pattern check, return bulge-chase-invariant-failure with the partial factors. This gives $\|E_j\|_F\le\alpha_{m_j}\|\widehat H_{j-1}\|_F$ when its $m_ju<1$ and range hypotheses hold. Apply the same certificate to every Hessenberg-initialization similarity. If any step lacks that certificate, retain the residual diagnostic and set the backward-error-certificate status to inconclusive.
5. Stop with Schur-computed when every complex block has size one, or every real block has size one or is a $2\times2$ block with negative characteristic-polynomial discriminant. If the target check fails when the sweep count reaches $N$, return budget-exhausted; in particular, with $N=0$ return Schur-computed only when the initialized matrix already has the target block structure. Return the partial matrix and factors on every failure or nonconvergence status.

Let $\widehat T$ be the final returned matrix. The output includes the product representation $Q$, residual matrix $R=Q^*AQ-\widehat T$ and its Frobenius norm as diagnostics, the exact orthogonality bound $0$ for that reflector product, the recorded deflation entries, and either the accumulated backward-error bound when all local certificates exist or certificate status inconclusive. A rounded dense matrix formed from $Q$ has its own orthogonality residual and is not asserted exactly unitary. The residual diagnostic does not itself give a forward eigenvalue bound. **Scalar execution order.** These conventions expand every arithmetic
expression below into a fixed finite scalar schedule; they do not execute the
exact theoretical representatives. Visit vector indices increasingly and matrix
columns increasingly, with row indices increasing within each column. Visit the
real component before the imaginary component. For a complex vector $z$, its
real-component list is $(\Re z_1,\Im z_1,\ldots,\Re z_r,\Im z_r)$.
Evaluate displayed assignments in their written order and nested operations
from the inside out, left operand before right operand. For inputs $a+ib$ and
$c+id$ with real components $a,b,c,d$, a complex product uses
rounded real products $ac,bd,ad,bc$, in that order, followed by the rounded real
subtraction $ac-bd$ and rounded imaginary addition $ad+bc$. Do not fuse
operations. Return immediately at the first failing primitive; indices refer
to this expanded order. Copies, sign changes and conjugations are exact.

For a scaled norm, first form every rounded component divided by the common
scale in list order. Then, in that same order, round each component square and
accumulate it: copy the first square to the accumulator, and round each
subsequent accumulator-plus-square addition. Use this same square-and-sum
schedule for the stored-vector squared norm $w$, without scaling. An empty
sum is exact zero and requests no primitive. Apply square root and rescaling
only at their prescribed subsequent stages. The two-component and
four-component norm calls use their displayed component lists in this order.

For the Householder dot row $d$, visit columns $j$ increasingly. For each
column visit $i=1,\ldots,r$, form the declared complex product
$\overline v_iB_{ij}$, copy the first product as the partial dot, then add each
later product by rounded real-component addition followed by rounded
imaginary-component addition. Finish all of $d$ before forming $p$ in
increasing row order, then all of $Z$ in the matrix order above, then all
entries of $B-Z$ in that order. Evaluate both components of the formation of
$v$ and every scalar scaling or division in real-then-imaginary order. A
separate block call uses already stored $v,\widehat\tau$ and the same
$d,p,Z,B-Z$ stages, omitting formation and target overwrite.

For a Givens application, visit columns increasingly and copy the two old
entries before changing either. Compute the upper output first, then the
lower output, each by its two products in written order followed by its
componentwise addition. Each of the prescribed two complex products uses
the six-operation schedule above, including a real coefficient viewed as a
complex number with zero imaginary component. Both outputs use the copied
old entries.
Perform an instructed target zero write only after these outputs. Right
applications execute the stated conjugate-transpose reduction with these
same conventions. No intermediate is reused across different expressions
unless explicitly stored by the procedure.

Set $\widehat\alpha=-\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\phi\widehat N)$ using real-scalar component multiplication, and $v=\operatorname{fl}(x-\widehat\alpha e_1)$. Compute $w$ by sequential summation of all $2r$ rounded real component squares of $v$, and $\widehat\tau=\operatorname{fl}(2/w)$. Compute $d=\operatorname{fl}(v^*B)$, $p=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\tau v)$, $Z=\operatorname{fl}(pd)$, and $\widehat B=\operatorname{fl}(B-Z)$. Return $C_+=[\widehat\alpha e_1\;\widehat B]$, writing exact zeros below the target diagonal, and store $v,\widehat\tau$. Its theoretical representative is $H(v)=I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$. For a separate block application omit the column overwrite. For a right step apply these instructions to the conjugate-transposed block and transpose back.

For a Givens target pair $(a,b)$, use the identity when $b=0$, including $(0,0)$.
